Re-dispatch design sketch (kept crate-local, owned root only): new module backend/crates/platform/audit-chain/src/external.rs — trait SealSignTransport (send seal_hash -> signature bytes, typed Unavailable error) + ExternalSealSigner { key_ref: 'external:<backend>:<key-id>', pinned trust anchors: Map<key_ref, VerifyingKey> injected at construction }. verify() consults ONLY the pinned anchors (unknown/unpinned stored key_ref -> Ok(false) => BadSignature verdict; NEVER derive key material from stored data); transport failure -> new SealSignError::Unavailable => seal pass Err (fail-closed, no in-memory fallback; run_tick already logs-and-continues per org so one org's signer outage cannot starve other tenants). Key custody: no key material may land in the repo — trust anchors arrive via injected config; the self-host signing daemon itself is a separate deliverable outside this crate's owned root (deploy manifests explicitly out of scope per brief).
